summary: Staging bastion-proxy: GCP WIF -> AWS STS token exchange failing, blocking CI cross-account debug
description:
Issue summary:
The internal bastion-proxy service in staging is failing to exchange a GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF) token for an AWS STS temporary credential when proxying CI and developer debug sessions into the staging AWS account. This prevents engineers and CI jobs from assuming necessary roles and blocks several debugging and integration pipelines.

Impact:
- Multiple CI pipelines that require cross-account access to staging are failing their integration step (approx. 8 failing runs in the last 24h).
- On-call SREs cannot escalate into the staging AWS account using the bastionless flow for investigative debugging.
- Not affecting production at this time, but raises a potential regression risk in the cross-cloud token exchange logic.

Environment / scope:
- Component: bastion-proxy (internal access broker) in staging - us-west (k8s cluster: staging-access-01).
- GCP identity provider: projects/9371223349/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/redwood-ci-pool.
- AWS account: arn:aws:iam::912345678901:role/staging-debug-assume-role.
- Affected services: CI jobs (github-actions), ad-hoc developer sessions routed through the proxy.

Reproduction steps (observed from CI job logs):
1) CI job requests temporary access by sending OIDC token (GCP WIF) to bastion-proxy endpoint /v1/assume-role.
2) Bastion-proxy validates token with GCP tokeninfo endpoint and attempts AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity to AWS STS with audience and session tags.
3) STS responds with 400/AccessDenied or 403 depending on token shape.
4) CI step fails with "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity - access denied" and the job aborts.

Observed behavior:
- Some tokens are rejected with a payload mismatch (aud != expected), others result in STS policy denial referencing session tags.
- Token exchange failures are intermittent: about 60% of attempts fail, 40% succeed. Failures cluster around tokens minted by a specific GKE node pool (staging-ci-pool-3).

Expected behavior:
- Bastion-proxy should consistently exchange WIF tokens for AWS STS credentials for approved identities in staging and return usable temporary credentials to the CI process.

Quick notes / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis A: GCP token audience configuration recently changed in the federated pool and some nodes are still minting tokens with an older audience string.
- Hypothesis B: Session tag size or permitted tag set exceeds the AWS role condition (policy expects specific tag keys), causing STS to reject requests for certain callers.
- Hypothesis C: A cached JWKS or token verification cache in bastion-proxy is stale for some GCP node metadata and yields bad token validation results.

Logs (excerpts):
logs: 2026-03-12T22:14:02Z bastion-proxy[assume-role] INFO incoming token from ci-runner-45: token_audience=//iam.googleapis.com/projects/9371223349/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/redwood-ci-pool/providers/github-provider

2026-03-12T22:14:02Z bastion-proxy[assume-role] WARN STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed: AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
	status code: 403, request id: 7f5c2b

2026-03-12T22:20:11Z bastion-proxy[assume-role] INFO incoming token from ci-runner-47: token_audience=//iam.googleapis.com/projects/9371223349/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/redwood-ci-pool/providers/github-provider
2026-03-12T22:20:11Z bastion-proxy[assume-role] INFO STS response: success - credentials issued (duration 3600s)

2026-03-12T23:01:30Z bastion-proxy[verify] ERROR token verification failed: jwks mismatch for key kid\"k_3\"
2026-03-12T23:01:30Z bastion-proxy[verify] DEBUG token payload: {sub: 'system:serviceaccount:ci:runner-243', aud: '//iam.googleapis.com/oldpool', tags: ['team:platform', 'session:debug'] }
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Noticed multiple failing CI runs that rely on bastion-proxy for cross-account access. Opening this ticket to coordinate root cause and restoration. Copying SRE and infra owners.
Samir Gupta (2026-03-10): Taking ownership. Initial guess: recent WIF provider change or JWKS cache. Will gather logs and pod-level metadata. ETA: investigating in next 4 hours.

Marta Li (SRE) (2026-03-11): I've seen similar flakiness when a workload identity pool was rotated; tokens minted right after rotation had an aud mismatch until node metadata refreshed. Can we confirm whether the pool was updated 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC?
Devops Bot (2026-03-11): Automated deploy pipeline recorded update: workloadIdentityPool 'redwood-ci-pool' provider 'github-provider' config changed in PR#8224 at 2026-03-11T01:58:43Z.

Samir Gupta (2026-03-11): Confirmed PR#8224 touched audience mapping. Reproduced failure from runner-243 whose node was last patched on 2026-03-11T02:30Z. Hypothesis: some nodes still present tokens with old audience string. Next: correlate failing runs with node patch times and rotate JWKS cache in bastion-proxy.

Eng Platform (2026-03-12): Noted that bastion-proxy adds session tags for 'team' and 'session' from caller metadata. AWS role policy for staging has a Condition requiring 'team' tag to be in allowed set; if tag missing or different, STS denies. We should validate tag presence too.
investigation_notes: Checked GCP admin audit logs: workloadIdentityPool provider config changed 2026-03-11T01:58:43Z (PR#8224).
Correlated failing CI jobs to node pool staging-ci-pool-3; nodes were patched 2026-03-11T02:20 - 02:45 UTC and some still returned older token audience until kubelet restart.
Observed two distinct failure signatures: (1) jwks mismatch / token aud mismatch; (2) sts denies referencing session tag mismatch. Both explain intermittent failures.

Replaying token from failing job via 'gcloud iam workload-identity-pools tokens exchange' reproduced STS AccessDenied when session tags included 'team:platform' but role condition allowed only 'team:infra' and 'team:services'.

Bastion-proxy config: it maps caller namespace -> team tag via a static mapping file in configmap; mapping had 'ci' -> 'platform' while staging IAM role expects 'ci' -> 'infra'. Mapping drift introduced after a config rollout 2026-02-20.
resolution_notes:
Immediate mitigations applied (2026-03-12):
- Rotated bastion-proxy's JWKS cache and restarted pods in staging-access-01 to pick up latest WIF provider keys.
- Hotfix applied to bastion-proxy configmap to align team tag mapping: changed 'ci' tag from 'platform' -> 'infra'.
- Added a temporary permissive AWS role policy override for staging-debug-assume-role to accept 'team:platform' for 24 hours to unblock CI until changes propagate.

Follow-ups / remediation:
- Create automated canary to detect WIF audience drift: add test that exchanges token and performs AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity on deploy. Owner: Samir (due 2026-03-20).
- Update runbook 'Bastionless Access Broker' with steps to rotate JWKS cache and validate node token audiences post WIF provider changes. Owner: SRE Docs (due 2026-03-17).
- Reconcile static tag mapping with IAM role condition expectations; move to a canonical source (terraform-managed mapping) to avoid manual drift. Owner: Infra Team (due 2026-04-01).
Status: bastion-proxy token exchange success rate returned to ~98% after JWKS rotation and config fix. CI runs resumed. Keeping ticket open for follow-ups and runbook updates.
